children: What was the main takeaway from the Federal Open Market Committee's decision on Wednesday to raise its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points?

params.linkText: Michael Kramer of Mott Capital Management

children: Lawrence Fuller: The Fed may have been bullied by the bond market into a symbolic quarter-point rate hike with the 2-year yield soaring, as well as the fear that no rate hike might drive 10-year yields higher, but I don't see this impacting inflation in any meaningful way.
Chairman Warsh now has to deal with the ire of President Trump, but he seems to be more concerned with the Fed's credibility than appeasing the president.

That's good for the market, although there has not been much relief in long-term rates, with the 10-year still hovering just below 5%. That's probably as much a reflection of strong economic growth as it is inflation fears, which should wane with the upcoming PCE report at month's end.
(Lawrence Fuller leads the SA investing group The Portfolio Architect.)
Leo Nelissen: It was a clear signal to the market, as all Fed members voted for a hike. They are telling us that inflation is a very serious problem.

The good news is that Warsh cited higher economic growth as a reason the economy can absorb a hike. Unfortunately, the part of the economy that is working is largely driven by AI, while housing, transportation, and many consumer sectors are suffering under elevated long-term rates and Iran War-related inflation. This isn’t normal demand-side inflation but supply-induced inflation.
Until these factors fade, every tightening risks derailing the economy, which is why markets have become so nervous.
(Leo Nelissen leads the SA investing group Main Street Alpha.)

Michael Kramer of Mott Capital Management: The Fed hiked rates by 25 bps, and in my view, this is probably only the first of many more hikes to come. Financial conditions remain too loose, and it will take more than one or two hikes to tighten them enough to bring PCE inflation back to 2%.
(Michael Kramer leads the SA investing group Reading the Markets.)
